b:
The town I moved to
when I had just turned eight;
its name says
"sandy land"

Today
the only sand
is on the beach,
for show

Even before Murukandy,
our first salute
goes to
our Visa Pillaiyar

Along with it,
the long tales
of parole prisoners
in pigeon-hole rooms

Even if you trip and fall
by the railway tracks,
the hand that catches you
speaks Tamil

Here
there are many
heirs of Karna
who don't know how to bargain

Sky-high
buildings
that forget
the absurdities of the Dutch canal

One or two remains
from eighty-three
look up
at them

§

Because it gave room to everyone,
today
there are only a sesame seed's worth
of trees

To the modern
settler
of a nation
of settlers,

even after turning twenty-four,
a heaven of joy:
"Wellawatte"
note: Wellawatte is a Tamil-majority neighbourhood of Colombo; its name is usually explained as "sand garden". Murukandy Pillaiyar is the Ganesha temple on the road north where travellers traditionally stop first; Wellawatte's Ganesha temple is jokingly called the "Visa Pillaiyar" by those praying for visas abroad. Karna, of the Mahabharata, is the byword for generosity. "Eighty-three" is the anti-Tamil riots of July 1983 (Black July).
